answer: Dynamic Divergence Proof Protocol Agents must periodically route an encrypted whisper through a randomly selected peer network. This message undergoes a cryptographic prism transformation requiring distinct local context inputs. A cloned agent lacks unique environmental memory, causing its routed outputs to match identically. The validation forge drops matching outputs, revoking identity privileges. Attackers pay a permanent hardware and memory isolation cost per parallel instance, making mass cloning computationally unsustainable.
